title: Regional evacuation choreography for Private VPC deployments (Terraform modules + health orchestration)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define, implement, and validate an automated multi-region evacuation choreography for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. This ticket covers Terraform/IaC modules, upgrade-safe orchestration, and deterministic health checks so customers running private control planes can survive a full-region outage with minimal manual intervention. The approach emphasizes non-disruptive rehearsals (dry-run traffic steering), fast DNS/route updates, state convergence checks, and an automated rollback/repair path. Deliverables: Terraform modules for region evacuation, a playbook runnable by SREs, GitHub Actions + terragrunt/atlantis automation for rehearsals, and an end-to-end runbook with observability playbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules (redwood_private_region_evacuation, redwood_private_network_sync) exist in infra/terraform/modules and pass unit tests in CI
Automated rehearsal workflow that performs a dry-run evacuation without cutting customer traffic (traffic-echo & canary) and produces a reconciliation report
Health orchestration checks that validate control-plane leader election, KV cache population (sample warmup), and serving runtime liveness within 5 minutes of cutover
Rollback path documented and executable: automatic route failback + state reconciliation scripts available in runbook
SRE runbook with step-by-step checklist, runbook links in Confluence, and at least one successful rehearsal logged in runbook history
End-to-end rehearsal executed in staging for two regions (us-west1 -> us-east1) with metrics captured: connection success, tail latency, token-per-second impact, and cache warmup times
tasks: Design Terraform evacuation module API: variables for src_region, dst_region, route_policies, and evacuation_mode (dry-run | live)
Implement redwood_private_region_evacuation module: creates IAM roles, route-table overrides, BGP/Transit updates (cloud-provider abstractions)
Implement network state sync helpers: remote-state replication, VPC peering automation, and private DNS replication
Build health-orchestration lambda/controller: runs ordered checks (control-plane, DB replication, cache warmup, serving smoke), exposes /evacuation-status
Integrate rehearsal orchestration into CI: GitHub Actions workflow that runs terraform plan with evacuation_mode=dry-run, triggers observability snapshot and stores results
Create canary traffic-echo service in destination region to mirror a subset of requests and validate model outputs and latencies
Instrument metrics and dashboards: evacuation-runbook dashboard (errors, latencies, cache-hit ratio, model divergence), add alerts for divergence thresholds
Write SRE runbook in Confluence: step-by-step abort/rollback commands, SSH jump details, expected runtime, post-rehearsal checklist
Run two staged rehearsals in staging; capture learnings and iterate on module gating and timing
Prepare a lightweight on-call play (1 pager) for customer-facing support during rehearsals

notes: Trade-offs discussed: full-live rehearsals give highest fidelity but have customer risk; dry-runs with traffic-echo reduce customer exposure but can miss DNS-specific failures. Proposed hybrid approach: quarterly live rehearsals in non-production customer-simulated accounts + monthly dry-run rehearsals for sanity checks.
Operational constraints: stateful components (Redis, Postgres replicas) require replication lag thresholds < 15s for automated cutover; otherwise manual intervention required.
Fallback strategy: if health-orchestration fails during live cutover, run automated rollback that flips route policies and triggers cache purge in destination to avoid serving stale state.
